title: Require a per-session token for notification click-exec
head: 4bd222e87660
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: findings: restore/history click-exec inconsistency; unfixed mint/readiness race; optional test improvement; doc, dependency and overlap notes

leads.summary: History replay re-arms click commands without checking the current session token
leads.consequence: A JSON record in notifications/history/ with execArgv (including one archived by an older shell session or one planted by a process that can write this state directory) becomes a runnable popup when showHistory is invoked. An expired restored popup is archived with its original execArgv at line 779, while a surviving finite-duration one is persisted with the original execArgv at line 789 before the in-memory value is cleared at line 798; either disk copy can later replay an action. This bypasses the new-session clearing on replay, so clicking the replay can execute an old or planted action without an omarchy-exec-token. Does not imply that an ordinary Flatpak can write the state directory. Strip or revalidate execArgv on every disk-to-popup and history-replay path, and clear it before any re-persist/archive of restored data.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; Opus F1; corroboration only; behavioural

leads.summary: A readable stale token produces an apparently successful but inert --exec notification
leads.consequence: The token file is never removed on shutdown, and token minting writes a new value only if mkdir and openssl succeed. If the shell starts with an old nonempty token file and minting fails (for example openssl rand returns nonzero, or the directory is readable but cannot be rewritten), its in-memory execToken remains empty. The sender checks readability/nonempty only, sends with the stale token and exits successfully while the new service drops its click command. A delayed sender also loses its action when the file was readable before a successful rotation but its notification arrives afterward. Thus --exec is not guaranteed to fail loudly when a live matching token cannot be obtained; important for one-shot first-run/migration and crash toasts.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; Opus F2; corroboration only; behavioural

leads.summary: Related open PR #12111 needs token-writer reconciliation before both changes can land
leads.consequence: Both open PRs independently modify the snapshotOf token argument and add a subprocess that writes the same $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy/notification-exec-token file. #12111 uses execSessionToken and writeExecTokenProc (started onCompleted), whereas this PR uses execToken and mintExecTokenProc (running:true). Their overlapping snapshotOf edits need manual resolution. If both writers are retained when resolving the conflict, the file contains only the last writer's token and the two in-memory properties can disagree; sending with the file's token is then rejected by whichever snapshot implementation uses the other value. Keep a single writer and in-memory token, and combine the independent image/hint-hardening changes deliberately.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; Opus F5; coordinator confirmed #12111 OPEN via gh; published as Overlapping PR note; factual

limits: No QML or live notification server was started. The isolated runs test only the sender and pure JS helpers; the history replay click and the mint-failure/new-shell scenario follow from pinned source and require an isolated QML/desktop scenario to measure in a real shell.

Quickshell v0.3.1 source at quickshell-src/server.cpp:177-195, notification.cpp:104-171 and notification.hpp:116-118 shows Notify accepts QVariantMap hints and stores custom keys. Actual QML-to-JavaScript QVariantMap property indexing on a real installed build was not measured; issue #8346 reports a suspected readback problem but is not treated here as a verified finding.

No new file, unit, device or group is introduced by #13312. The repository contains no PKGBUILD; install/omarchy-base.packages lists jq and quickshell, and install/omarchy-other.packages lists base. An explicit openssl entry is not present, but its transitive availability on all supported images was not proven, so no package-missing issue is claimed.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** For newly received notifications, the token gate works as described. `execArgvFromHints` returns the argv only when the expected token is non-empty and the `omarchy-exec-token` hint matches it exactly. The check runs on receive, on in-place replacements and on do-not-disturb writes. Quickshell 0.3.1 replaces hints wholesale on update, so a `replaces_id` update cannot reuse an earlier valid token. `omarchy-notification-send --exec` attaches the token, and its callers are all host-side scripts. The new sender and JavaScript tests pass at the head and fail against the base code, as intended.

Two parts of the second commit do not fully do what the PR describes. Both respond to points raised on the earlier PR #12912.

### Restored toasts lose their click action, but history replay still runs persisted argv

`restorePopups` clears `execArgv` only on the in-memory row ([`Service.qml:798`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/4bd222e876601136d37bc226fa24ccbaf5f33636/shell/plugins/notifications/Service.qml#L798)). The popup file keeps it:

- normal popups are re-persisted with `execArgv` just before the clear (lines 787-793);
- critical popups (duration 0) are not rewritten at all.

When the toast leaves the screen, the file moves to `history/`. `showHistory` (Super + Shift + Alt + comma) replays it through `historyEntry`, which copies `execArgv` ([`NotificationLogic.js:256`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/4bd222e876601136d37bc226fa24ccbaf5f33636/shell/plugins/notifications/NotificationLogic.js#L256)), and a click runs it through `invokePopupDefault`.

```text
popup file on disk (execArgv kept) --restore--> on-screen row: execArgv = ""   (click only dismisses)
                                   \--dismiss--> history/ --showHistory--> execArgv restored  (click runs argv)
```

**Impact:**
- **Legitimate toasts lose their action on every shell restart.** Every update run restarts the shell. On a fresh install, clicking "Update System" leaves the critical "Learn Keybindings" toast on screen, but its click then only dismisses it. Crash and pending-migration toasts behave the same way. Before this PR, the docs said a restored toast "clicks through exactly like a live one".
- **Pre-upgrade forged entries remain runnable** through history replay (restore-then-dismiss, or entries already in `history/`). This needs an entry forged before the upgrade plus a later click from history.
- The new docs reason ("the token is session-scoped") does not explain the clear. Argv persisted since this change was already validated on receipt and is never checked against the token again; only pre-token entries need clearing.

In an isolated Node run of the head `NotificationLogic.js`, a pre-upgrade forged record and a token-validated record both produced runnable argv through `historyRows` + `parseExecArgv`. The QML ordering above comes from source inspection; no live shell was run.

**Suggested change (untested):** Mark token-validated entries when persisting, for example `execVerified: true` beside a non-empty `execArgv`. Then blank `execArgv` in `parsePopupFiles` for any record without the mark (set the mark after `popupEntry` and check it before, since `popupEntry` and `historyEntry` rebuild entries with fixed fields). This strips pre-token entries on both the restore and the history paths, keeps validated actions across restarts (as step 4 of #8433 proposed) and makes the unconditional `entry.execArgv = ""` unnecessary. A smaller fix is to apply the same clear in the history path and persist the cleared value, at the cost of the legitimate actions.

### The startup race between token minting and notification readiness remains

The PR says starting the mint with `running: true` makes the token exist "before early --exec senders race the bus claim" ([`Service.qml:424-428`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/4bd222e876601136d37bc226fa24ccbaf5f33636/shell/plugins/notifications/Service.qml#L424-L428)). In the Quickshell v0.3.1 source, `Process` only launches its child in the post-reload pass (`process.cpp:41-48,180-183`). The `NotificationServer` bus-name claim and the `IpcHandler` go live in that same pass. `execToken` is set only after the child exits. The ordering is therefore the same as starting the mint from `Component.onCompleted`, and the guard `if (service.execToken)` at line 893 cannot be true when it runs.

`omarchy-notification-wait` (IPC ping + `GetServerInformation`) and the `NameHasOwner` check in `omarchy-restart-shell` still do not wait for the token. The token is also re-minted on every shell start.

Runs of the head sender (busctl stub, synthetic runtime dir) plus the head receiver logic:

| State at send time | Result |
|---|---|
| Token file missing (first shell start of a login) | `--exec` exits 1 and busctl is not called: no toast at all |
| Previous shell's token still on disk | Toast sent; the receiver drops the click argv |
| Empty file (read between truncate and write) | exits 1, no toast |

**Impact:** Callers that send right after the readiness checks can lose the toast or its action. `omarchy-migrate-notify` falls back to journal text. A crash toast from `omarchy-crash-watch` is not re-sent. Post-update invitation hooks mark themselves done before sending, so a lost toast there is not retried. The window is probably short, but the PR presents the ordering as fixed and nothing orders it. Frequency on a live shell was not measured.

**Suggested change (untested):** Create the `NotificationServer` only after the mint has finished (for example behind a `Loader` gated on a mint-finished flag). Then, whenever the mint succeeds, the existing bus-name readiness checks also mean the token file and `execToken` are current. Minting once per login session (only when the file is missing or empty, written to a temp file and `mv`'d into place) would also remove the stale-token and empty-read cases across restarts.

### Smaller notes

**Optional test improvement:** The new `Service.qml` assertions only check that strings are present. Two mutants pass the head suite:
- The mint Process set to `running: false`. The regex `/id: mintExecTokenProc[\s\S]*?running: true/` (test line 776) also matches the text "(running: true)" in the comment at `Service.qml:890`.
- Restore no longer waiting for the token. The "restores popups only after the token" assertion only checks that the strings `startRestoreAfterToken` and `entry.execArgv = ""` exist, not where the restore is called.

Anchoring the regex to the `Process` block and asserting the call inside `onStreamFinished` would catch both.

**Documentation:**
- The comment at `NotificationLogic.js:144-146` still says the argv keeps restored toasts clickable.
- `docs/notifications.md:150-152` still presents `omarchy-notification-wait` as enough for senders near a shell restart, which does not hold for `--exec`.
- Test description typo: "untoked".

**Dependency:** `openssl` is not listed in `install/omarchy-base.packages`. It is very likely present on Arch as a dependency of core packages; this was not verified. Without it, the mint fails closed and every `--exec` click is disabled.

**Overlapping PR:** Open PR #12111 still contains a separate exec-token writer for the same `notification-exec-token` file on the same files. Landing both as they stand would conflict or leave two token writers.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head and base source, including the Quickshell v0.3.1 `Process` and notification server source. The PR's two test suites ran at head and base, plus mutants of the head. The head sender ran with a busctl stub and a synthetic runtime dir. The head and base `NotificationLogic.js` ran in Node, with synthetic records. The tests of the `--exec` callers ran at head and base; they stub the sender. There was no live Quickshell, D-Bus, click or Flatpak run, and the startup window was not measured on a live shell. The QML ordering claims rest on source inspection.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
